articles.title: Trump tells voters ahead of midterms: ‘Pretend I’m on the ballot’
articles.summary: President Trump again urged Americans on Wednesday to cast their vote as if he was “on the ballot” this November. “I see it all the time, that when Trump’s on the ballot, they win,” the president told Fox News’s Trey Gowdy. “When he’s out of the ballot, the people don’t go to vote, and I’m…
articles.body:
President Trump again urged Americans on Wednesday to cast their vote as if he was “on the ballot” this November.

“I see it all the time, that when Trump’s on the ballot, they win,” the president told Fox News’s Trey Gowdy. “When he’s out of the ballot, the people don’t go to vote, and I’m asking the people … to get out and vote. Pretend I’m on the ballot.”

The president’s interview with Gowdy will air on “Sunday Night in America” in full this weekend. His comments come as the Republican Party looks to ramp up efforts to engage voters ahead of the midterm elections, which are now less than 10 weeks away.

Trump previously invoked this same messaging tactic during a rally for Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.) last week. The senator, sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.), beat challenger Rep. Ralph Norman (S.C.) in the state’s Republican primary runoff for the Senate Tuesday by narrow margins — despite wielding an endorsement from the president.

“What I want you to do is pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot,” Trump told the crowd of supporters, warning that Democrats would “impeach” him if they regained a majority in Congress.

The president will attend both days of the GOP’s upcoming midterm convention in Dallas next month as part of this turnout effort.

House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said during a campaign event in Sinton, Texas, on Thursday that Trump will “look right into the camera” and declare he is “on the ballot” at the event.

“Because even though his name isn’t … his administration, his legacy, the America First agenda is,” Johnson said. “We got to get people to turn out.”

Fox News host Sean Hannity raised a similar talking point during a Wednesday broadcast.

“Let me explain this: He is on the ballot because if we don’t get Republicans in the House and Senate, all progress in this country will come to a screeching halt,” Hannity told his viewers.

He warned that a Democratic majority in Congress would make the impeachment of Trump and other Republican officials a “top agenda item.”

A wave of unfavorable public polling amid the Iran war and cost of living issues have raised concerns about the GOP’s success rate at the ballot box this November. Trump had a net approval rating of negative 19.5 percentage points, according to a Thursday update in Silver Bulletin’s polling tracker .

Decision Desk HQ places the odds that Democrats retake the House majority this year at 67 percent, while projecting there is a 52 percent chance Republicans retain their control of the Senate.

articles.title: Jake Reiner opens up on parents’ death, brother’s arrest in first interview
articles.summary: “My parents had unconditional love for all three of us,” he added, also noting the toll of his brother’s imprisonment.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Jake Reiner said that he is constantly reminded of his circumstances in his first interview since his brother, Nick Reiner, allegedly murdered their parents.

“It’s been 8 months. It feels like 8 years at the same time. And it also feels like 8 minutes,” he told KABC-TV’s Mark Cota-Robles in a Thursday preview of the interview on “Good Morning America,” according to People Magazine . “Because every moment that I wake up, I’m reminded of my reality.”

Actor and director Rob Reiner and his wife, photographer and producer Michele Singer Reiner , were found stabbed to death in their Southern California home in December 2025. In the interview, Jake Reiner recalled the moment his sister, Romy Reiner, called to report what happened: “Romy told me our dad was dead and then she said, ‘I can’t find mom.’”

“My parents had unconditional love for all three of us,” he added, also noting the toll of his brother’s imprisonment. “Yeah. I mean, he’s in jail … I physically lost my parents. And then Nick was arrested. And now it’s me and Romy.”

Nick Reiner was indicted by a grand jury earlier this month and now faces charges including two counts of murder with the special circumstance allegations of multiple murders and murder by means of lying in wait. The indictment will expedite the case to a jury, bypassing a preliminary hearing.

Reiner had previously been charged with first-degree murder, but prosecutors secured a special circumstance enhancement that alleges he was lying in wait to murder them. The special circumstance can increase potential penalties in the sentencing phase of a trial to the death penalty or life in prison without the possibility of parole.

Reiner, who lived with his parents, previously pleaded not guilty to killing them. In the past, he had spoken openly about his struggles with drug addiction and periods of homelessness and co-wrote a movie inspired by his struggles with his father.

articles.title: Controllers warned Marine One pilots of communications issue days before near-miss with jet, NTSB says
articles.summary: Air traffic controllers in Washington and the pilots of President Donald Trump’s helicopter met to discuss communication issues one week before a jet and the chopper were allowed to take off at the same time, the National Transportation Safety Board said Thursday.
articles.body: Air traffic controllers in Washington and the pilots of President Donald Trump’s helicopter met to discuss communication issues one week before a jet and the chopper were allowed to take off at the same time, the National Transportation Safety Board said Thursday. Both sides met to discuss the failures in communications and agreed to an alternative for such occasions — but that method was also unsuccessful on the day of the Aug. 4 incident at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, the National Transportation Safety Board’s preliminary report shows. Having both in the air at the same time seemed to violate safety procedures put in place after last year’s midair collision near the busy airport that killed 67 people, but officials stressed the president was never in danger. The Pentagon also has a longstanding agreement with the FAA to provide controllers with a three-minute warning before the president’s helicopter takes off that predates last year’s crash. The FAA decided after an airliner collided with an Army Black Hawk helicopter on Jan. 29, 2025, that all takeoffs and landings at the airport would be halted anytime a helicopter passes by on a conflicting route. The airspace near the White House and Reagan is heavily congested with military and commercial aircraft. The FAA has acknowledged that the helicopter and airliner briefly got too close before the two aircraft started to move away from each other. The airplane quickly climbed above the helicopter after Marine One’s pilots saw the plane and paused until it safely left the area. Tower audio suggests that the air traffic controller may not have realized that Trump’s helicopter was getting ready to head to Andrews Air Force Base with the president aboard that day until right as Marine One was taking off. A recording posted by ATC.com showed the Marine One pilot telling the tower that the helicopter was “three minutes to life” just like the 2013 agreement between the FAA and the military calls for. But the air traffic controller said that transmission appeared broken and unreadable on his end, so the controller seemed surprised a few minutes later when the helicopter took off. “Uh, Marine One, you said, uh, you’re proceeding as briefed?” the controller asked before giving the helicopter directions and commenting, “OK, no three minutes, roger, proceed as briefed.” After the controller warned the helicopter about the plane taking off, the Marine One pilot said he saw the traffic and declared, “We’ll be doing a momentary delay.” After last year’s midair collision, it became clear that poor communication between air traffic controllers and the military had been a longstanding issue. During a congressional hearing, it came out that a hotline connecting the Pentagon to the tower at Reagan hadn’t been working for more than three years, and the FAA hadn’t even realized it.

articles.title: Chuck Edwards writes letter defending himself against sexual harassment allegations
articles.summary: North Carolina Rep. Chuck Edwards (R) on Wednesday issued a letter to fellow lawmakers denouncing the Ethics Committee report that found he engaged in “persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct” toward two younger female staff members. “The report repeatedly relies upon interactions that it says ‘could be interpreted as romantic.’ But something that could be interpreted…
articles.body:
North Carolina Rep. Chuck Edwards (R) on Wednesday issued a letter to fellow lawmakers denouncing the Ethics Committee report that found he engaged in “persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct” toward two younger female staff members.

“The report repeatedly relies upon interactions that it says ‘could be interpreted as romantic.’ But something that could be interpreted as romantic is worlds apart from establishing an unwanted sexual advance. An affectionate friendship is not a sexual proposition. A gift is not sexual misconduct. A compliment is not sexual misconduct. Poetry is not sexual misconduct,” read the letter to his colleagues first obtained by NOTUS .

“Socializing with a colleague is not sexual misconduct. Caring deeply about someone with whom you have worked and come to know for years is not sexual misconduct. Yet individual acts that were not themselves prohibited were gathered together, assigned the most damaging possible interpretation, and then used collectively to support a conclusion far more serious than the underlying evidence,” Edwards said in the letter.

The letter comes as the full House is preparing to vote on the Ethics Committee’s recommendation to censure Edwards. The vote could be held as early as next week.

The Hill has reached out to Edwards’s office for comment.

Investigators on the Ethics Committee reviewed roughly 1,500 pages of evidence and interviewed 16 witnesses. The complaints detailed lavish gifts, jewelry, a trip to New York City to see “Hamilton,” personal late-night text messages, comments on the staffers’ appearances and an instance where Edwards read an original poem at a going-away party.

The committee stated it did not find that Edwards engaged in explicit sexual activity or quid pro quo propositions but concluded his behavior violated House standards against sexual harassment and created a hostile work environment.

Earlier this month, Edwards dropped his bid for reelection over the allegations of sexual assault. State Rep. Jennifer Balkcom (R-N.C.) picked up the torch after being tapped by the 11th Congressional District’s Republican committee to replace Edwards on the ballot.

Edwards has urged his colleagues to determine if the report presented by the Ethics Committee shows evidence establishing misconduct or “inference being used to bridge the absence of evidence.”

In his letter, he writes that there are no House rules prohibiting members of Congress and staff from being friends, spending social time together or “genuinely and deeply caring” about each other.

“Those distinctions matter. Otherwise, perfectly permissible conduct can become evidence of wrongdoing simply by accumulating enough examples of it and assigning them an improper motive,” the letter reads.

“Ten permissible acts do not become misconduct merely because they are placed together in ten paragraphs,” it continues.

Edwards writes some gifts were used as “job-related tools” and argues that he gave to both male and female staffers “olive oil, cookware, rum, Kennedy Center tickets and even a handgun.”

Meanwhile, the lawmaker writes staffers also gave him “a custom-made NFL jersey, bourbon and whiskey, custom throw blankets, whiskey glasses, a taxidermy animal, a planned skydiving trip, wall plaques and other gifts.”

articles.title: Trump’s approval ratings endure a cruel summer
articles.summary: President Trump is enduring a difficult summer in public opinion polls, with his falling approval rating deepening concerns for Republicans that they could lose the House and Senate majorities this fall. Trump has hit record lows in various polls, including a 33 percent approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll this week. In the latest Economist/YouGov…
articles.body:
President Trump is enduring a difficult summer in public opinion polls, with his falling approval rating deepening concerns for Republicans that they could lose the House and Senate majorities this fall.

Trump has hit record lows in various polls, including a 33 percent approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll this week.

In the latest Economist/YouGov survey, Trump is exiting August with a 33 percent approval rating, a new low for him in that poll.

Trump’s polling in the Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) average did see a slight increase Thursday, reaching 39.2 percent.

Still, this average marked the second-lowest released by DDHQ since May, when Trump averaged 38 percent. The polling average also found that 57.5 percent disapproved of the president.

DDHQ chief elections analyst Geoffrey Skelley told The Hill that Trump’s low polling across the board is largely due to his handling of the economy, which had been among his strongest issues entering both terms, and the unpopularity of the Iran war.

“That to me looms as a big problem, not because it’s foreign policy necessarily,” Skelley said. “It’s because of the domestic impact and how it connects to people’s economic frustrations, and the fact that’s playing into that is, I think, the big concern on that front.”

That is a problem for GOP candidates on the ballot for the House and the Senate this year.

DDHQ is projecting that Democrats will retake the House majority in November, putting the odds at 67 percent. The GOP has a 52 percent chance of retaining the Senate majority despite Trump’s poor numbers, per DDHQ.

Democrats would need to gain four seats to win back the Senate, which seemed like a tall order at the beginning of the year. Now. Democrats think the majority is in reach, in large part because of the lack of wind in Trump’s sails as reflected in public opinion polls.

Skelley noted the Democratic optimism in his comments, saying Democrats are “extremely animated.” He said the figures have Democrats thinking their voters will be more motivated to come out and vote this fall in midterm elections that generally have a lower turnout than presidential years.

“So they’re looking very enthusiastic to turn out, and the midterms have lower turnout,” he said.

Republicans, on the other hand, have reason to worry their voters will come out in droves given that Trump is less popular and is not on the ballot.

Skelley said the two big problems for Trump and the GOP are” whether or not turnout is going to be decent enough among the base, or people just so dissatisfied and frustrated with the status quo that some of them don’t turn out.”

He also said the GOP has to worry about losing the swing voters that can decide a close election.

Trump’s numbers are lower than they were in his first term.

Trump’s approval rating from Gallup, which no longer measures presidential approval ratings, at the end of his first term was 34 percent . That left him averaging a 41 percent job approval during his first term.

The last time Trump’s approval rating wasn’t underwater was March 3, 2025, when DDHQ found his average approval to be at 48.1 percent compared with a disapproval of 47.7 percent.

When asked by The Hill to comment on the president’s approval rating, a White House official referred to Trump’s Truth Social post on Monday, when he accused Democrats of “going CRAZY with Fake Polls.”

“They’re putting them out at levels never seen before,” Trump wrote.

In that post, Trump also argued that real polls show him with stronger numbers, but he did not point to any specific polls showing him with stronger numbers.

“They’re called, ‘Demoralization Operations,’ where they try to demoralize Republicans so that they don’t go out and vote — But the actual Polls are tremendous, and the Spirit in our Country has never been higher,” Trump wrote. “We’re winning against EVERYONE, including Iran, whose Country is in Economic and Military Death Spiral.”

Trump’s numbers heading into the 2026 midterm elections are lower than they were at the same point in his term in 2018, when they typically stood around 40 percent. They reached their highest point at the start of the pandemic, at 49 percent in April and May 2020, according to Gallup.

In the 2018 midterms, the GOP ended up losing the House majority, but it gained two seats in the Senate.

Polling conducted by Reuters/Ipsos released in mid-August 2018 found Trump’s approval rating was at 41 percent among all Americans, with 53 percent saying they disapproved. Eight years later and Trump’s approval, based on data from the same polling partners , is 8 points below that, at 33 percent.

Trump’s most recent numbers are also lower than former President Biden’s in August 2022, when Reuters/Ipsos found Biden had an approval rating of 40 percent, its highest point since it dipped to 36 percent in May 2022.

The GOP won back the House majority in the 2022 midterms but did not win back the Senate majority. Its gains in the House were also not as high as many in the GOP had forecast at the time.

Skelley said Democrats were helped that year by voters who “somewhat” disapproved of Biden in polls.

“One of the reasons why things didn’t go as badly for Democrats, even though Joe Biden’s approval rating was bad, is that people who somewhat disapproved of Biden did not vote very strongly,” Skelley said. “In fact, they went narrowly for Democrats, according to the exit poll. It was close to 50-50, and that was a change because, historically, voters who somewhat disapproved voted for the out party by a pretty strong margin.”

Trump’s second-term approval rating is low by the standards of his other predecessors since former President Reagan, according to Gallup . Most of these presidents saw declining approval ratings during the first years of their presidencies, but Reagan and former Presidents Clinton and Obama all had higher approval ratings compared with Trump’s between late July and early August of the second year of each term.

Obama, for example, had a 47 percent approval rating in August 2010 and 44 percent in July 2014. Reagan’s and Clinton’s are more comparable with similar approval ratings in July 1982 and July 1994, respectively, and the same 63 percent approval rating in July 1986 for Reagan and early August 1998 for Clinton.

Father-and-son former presidents George H.W. Bush and George W. Bush both saw their approval ratings plunge later in their presidencies. But George W. Bush’s was lower than his father’s, entering the 2006 midterms with a 36 percent approval rating, compared with 65 percent ahead of the 2002 midterms.

The younger Bush left office with a 34 percent approval rating, but not before it hit 25 percent, the third-lowest Gallup job approval since former President Truman’s 22 percent in February 1952 and former President Nixon’s 24 percent in July and August 1974, just ahead of his resignation.

Skelley said Trump is facing an unpopular war, as were Truman, Nixon and George W. Bush toward the end of their presidencies, but the country is far more polarized than it was in the 1950s, 1970s and 2000s. He is skeptical, however, that Trump’s approval rating will sink below 30 percent.

“There are just more people who may be committed to sticking with a president of either party than they would have been in the past, so that makes it harder for me to imagine. I think, really, in this day and age, what it would take is something akin to what we saw in 2008,” Skelley said, referring to the Great Recession.

Skelley said Trump could turn things around and see his approval rise if the Iranian conflict sees a conclusion before the midterms and economic conditions improve as a result. But the president has a shrinking window of time to see that turnaround.

“You’re running out of time for things to notably change,” he said. “And that’s, to me, the main problem, and if some underlying conditions start to change, they have to be felt. And so there’s always a delay in how things are felt in terms of economic conditions or other, you know, other things of that nature.”

articles.title: US President Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’
articles.summary: The rebrand comes as the US and Canada engage in a cross-border trade war after Trump increased tariffs last week.
articles.body:
Amid a spiraling trade war with Canada, United States President Donald Trump says he is renaming a body of water shared between the two countries.

At a Tuesday news conference in the Oval Office, Trump signed an executive order that changes the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America. The president told reporters the name change will take place “effective immediately”.

When asked what message he was trying to send Canada with the renaming, Trump criticised the country’s trade relationship with US, claiming it “has been ripping us off for a long time”.

“Well, they haven’t treated us well. The Canadian officials have treated us very badly. They’re nasty people,” Trump said.

“So the lake change – the Lake of America – was something I’ve been thinking about for a long time, actually,” he added.

It’s not the first time Trump has renamed a geographical feature that has a name with ties to a neighboring country.

Upon returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump immediately signed an executive order that rebranded the “Gulf of Mexico” as the “Gulf of America”.

In the order, Trump justified the name change by stating the gulf “has long been an integral asset to our once burgeoning Nation and has remained an indelible part of America”.

However, cartographers and governments have used “Gulf of Mexico” for nearly 500 years, long before the US officially became a country.

Despite sharing a name with Canada’s most populous province, Lake Ontario took its official designation from the Huron Indigenous people’s word “oniatarí:io”, which translates to “lake of shining waters”. The province, founded in 1867, took its name from the body of water.

During Thursday’s Oval Office signing, Trump teased possible America-themed name changes for other bodies of water bordering the US.

“We have a gulf and we have a lake. Now all we need is an ocean,” Trump said. “So maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and or the Pacific. Maybe we’ll change them both.”

articles.title: Mamdani stands by DSA insider accused of stiffing landlord during $1.4M townhome makeover
articles.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani twice declined to distance himself from NYC-DSA co-chair Gustavo Gordillo, who faces a pending rent case and scrutiny over his union credentials and family townhouse renovation.
articles.body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani repeatedly declined to distance himself from embattled New York City Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) co-chair Gustavo Gordillo, after being pressed on allegations that the DSA leader failed to pay thousands in rent on a Crown Heights apartment while his family spent a reported $1.4 million renovating the NYC townhouse where he lives—a contrast critics say is difficult to square with the anti-landlord, rent-abolitionist socialist housing agenda he helps champion. Mamdani said Sunday that people working for a "more affordable life" and a "fairer life" for New Yorkers "should be welcomed into this work." When asked again Monday whether Gordillo should step down and whether he condemned allegations that Gordillo lied about his employment, the mayor said he welcomed anyone committed to making New York "a city that everyone can belong to." Meanwhile, asked directly whether he condemned Gordillo’s alleged actions and lying, Mamdani ended the exchange: "Thank you very much." Gordillo, an Ivy League graduate who as a NYC-DSA co-chair met weekly with Mamdani and his campaign manager as the group coordinated fundraising, field and communications efforts, later served on Mamdani’s Economic Development & Workforce Development transition committee, according to public reporting. He is named in a pending Brooklyn Housing Court case, in which a former landlord alleges Gordillo failed to pay $5,000 in rent on a $2,500-a-month Crown Heights apartment, while his family's townhouse was undergoing its $1.4 million in renovations, according to the New York Post. Gordillo's family reportedly bought the Bed-Stuy townhouse in 2019 for $935,000, while Gordillo’s father has said it is for Gordillo and his brother to live in. SOCIALIST BIGWIG BLASTS THE WEALTHY WHILE LIVING IN $1.4M BROOKLYN BROWNSTONE WITH EYEBROW-RAISING BACKSTORY "The Democratic Socialists of America have become the Double Standards of America — demanding transparency, fairness, and accountability from everyone else while ignoring serious questions about one of their own," Rev. Kevin McCall, a Brooklyn pastor who also assists tenants in New York City Housing Authority complexes, told the New York Post. "The allegations surrounding NYC chapter co-chair Gustavo Gordillo raise troubling questions about whether he misled working-class New Yorkers about where he lived, how he obtained housing, and his labor credentials. DSA leaders and elected officials must answer these questions publicly and call for Gordillo’s resignation," the Reverend added. NEW YORK CITY MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI STRUGGLES TO DEFINE 'WORKING CLASS' Neither Mamdani's office, the NYC-DSA nor Gordillo, responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. The housing case involving Gordillo remains pending and no judgment has been issued. Questions about Gordillo’s working-class credentials were also central to Monday’s exchange between Mamdani and reporters about Gordillo. The International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers told the New York Post that its Joint Apprentice Training Committee terminated Gordillo’s electrician apprenticeship in March after a "prolonged absence from and failure to participate in required work and classes." FRUSTRATED BLUE-COLLAR UNION BOSSES RIP SOCIALIST POLITICIANS, WARN OF LABOR EXODUS FROM DEM PARTY The New York Post reported that Gordillo later sought and received approval for a $95,000 annual salary from NYC-DSA without disclosing the termination to members. The outlet also reported that the Bed-Stuy renovation used nonunion contractors and was hit with a city stop-work order over permit issues—prompting further criticism of a DSA leader who has cast himself as a union electrician and advocate for working people.
